rationale: A human Parkinson cohort gives inconclusive associations with binary hyposmia. The PRKN family report has no comparison of smell change. Concentrated green-tea extract caused olfactory lesions after gavage in mice, while intranasal white tea improved odor tasks in a separate stress model. The routes, tea preparations and outcomes leave the direction with brewed green tea in Parkinson unresolved.

The Parkinson case included a cumin-containing tablet within a combined regimen and reported less OFF in percentage terms with the ordinal score unchanged. There are no diary hours or an ingredient-specific comparison. Rat pharmacokinetics and patent examples concern other drugs and concentrated exposures. Ground cumin effects on daily OFF time remain unresolved.

The isolated dried-pepper attention comparison did not establish a difference. An Alzheimer mixture reports concentration improvement without an available item-level comparison, and a separate canine extract mixture improved spatial attention. Neither mixture isolates pepper. The direction for cracked black pepper and Parkinson attention remains unresolved.
